text:
Noah: hi team, first week and hit a weird one. i can’t reach our k8s API at 10.96.0.1 when on split-tunnel VPN from my home lab (i run a local kubernetes on 10.96.0.0/12). office network and corp laptop work fine. ubuntu 24.04, wg-quick. any ideas?

Riley (Infra): welcome! sounds like an overlapping subnet conflict your local k8s cluster is using the same service CIDR as our cluster (10.96.0.0/12). check `ip route get 10.96.0.1` and `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'` to confirm which endpoint you're hitting.

Noah: `ip route get 10.96.0.1` shows via 192.168.1.1 (local) not the wg0 interface. `kubectl` points to https://10.96.0.1:443.

Dina (SRE): yep overlap. two practical options: 1) change your local cluster service CIDR (if ephemeral) to avoid 10.96/12, or 2) add a host route so 10.96.0.1 goes via wg0: `sudo ip route add 10.96.0.1/32 dev wg0` (forces the API traffic over the VPN), or 3) use `kubectl proxy --address=127.0.0.1 --accept-hosts=.*` on a bastion and `ssh -L 8001:10.96.0.1:443 rdw-bastion` to tunnel.

Noah: added the host route and `kubectl get pods` works now. changing local cluster is messy because i use it for hardware testing.

Riley (Infra): good call. we'll add an onboarding note about "service CIDR overlap" and a short script that detects local routes to corp service CIDRs and suggests a `ip route add` or kubeadm remap.

Onboard Bot: Created INF-802: "New-hire network: detect service CIDR overlap with local k8s and suggest fixes" assigned to Infrastructure.

Noah: leaving this thread since others with home labs might hit same thing. thanks everyone :pray:
